titleEn: I research play – and here’s why recess is much more important than just a fun break
titleZh: 课间休息的意义，远不止好玩这么简单
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: School recess has long been considered a standard part of children’s education in the United States. But it’s more than just a fun break from sitting at a desk.
paragraphs.zh: 在美国，学校的课间休息一直被认为是儿童教育的一个标准组成部分，但它不仅仅是坐在书桌前的一个有趣的休息。

paragraphs.en: Daily recess is necessary for supporting young children and adolescents’ learning, as well as their physical and mental health.
paragraphs.zh: 每日课间休息对于支持幼儿和青少年的学习及其身心健康是必要的。

paragraphs.en: It’s so important that the American Academy of Pediatrics notes that reducing the amount of time set aside for playing, running and exploring in order to fit in more academic work could actually be counterproductive.
paragraphs.zh: 这一点非常重要，美国儿科学会指出，为了适应更多的学术工作而减少用于玩耍、跑步和探索的时间实际上可能适得其反。

paragraphs.en: But in recent decades many schools have cut back on recess, which many states do not require.
paragraphs.zh: 但近几十年来，许多学校减少了课间休息，而许多州并不要求课间休息。

paragraphs.en: As a scholar who researches childhood play, I have studied and witnessed the benefits of play in children’s lives, including the significant social, emotional and cognitive impacts it has on students’ overall well-being.
paragraphs.zh: 作为一名研究儿童游戏的学者，我研究并见证了游戏在儿童生活中的好处，包括它对学生整体幸福感的重大社会，情感和认知影响。

paragraphs.en: The many benefits of recess
paragraphs.zh: 休息的诸多好处

paragraphs.en: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends that children and adolescents get at least 60 minutes of physical activity per day.
paragraphs.zh: 美国疾病控制和预防中心建议儿童和青少年每天至少进行60分钟的体育活动。

paragraphs.en: The CDC also defines recess as a “regularly scheduled period in the school day for physical activity and play that is monitored by trained staff or volunteers.”
paragraphs.zh: 疾病预防控制中心还将课间休息定义为“在学校一天中定期安排的由训练有素的工作人员或志愿者监测的体育活动和玩耍时间”。

paragraphs.en: Recess can look different across various schools – while some kids play outside on play structures or in grassy fields, others might play indoors during inclement weather.
paragraphs.zh: 课间休息在不同的学校看起来是不同的--有些孩子在户外的游乐设施或草地上玩耍，有些孩子在恶劣的天气下可能在室内玩耍。

paragraphs.en: Research also shows, for example, that children living in lower-income communities have fewer opportunities than their peers in higher-income communities to play outside.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，研究还表明，生活在低收入社区的儿童比生活在高收入社区的同龄人在户外玩耍的机会更少。

paragraphs.en: Unlike physical education classes or participating in organized sports, recess gives students the time to engage in physical activity and interact with their peers however they like.
paragraphs.zh: 与体育课或参加有组织的运动不同，课间休息让学生有时间从事体育活动，并与他们的同龄人互动，无论他们喜欢。

paragraphs.en: This time for unstructured play can offer much-needed relief from the mental focus that students need to maintain throughout the school day. It can also support their cognitive development and overall emotional and physical well-being.
paragraphs.zh: 这段时间的非结构化游戏可以为学生提供急需的缓解，使他们能够在整个学校中保持精神集中。它还可以支持他们的认知发展以及整体情感和身体健康。

paragraphs.en: Research also consistently shows that giving children breaks each day for recess has immense benefits for their mental health and the executive functioning skills that support academic achievement.
paragraphs.zh: 研究还一致表明，每天给孩子休息时间对他们的心理健康和支持学业成就的执行功能技能有巨大的好处。

paragraphs.en: This includes benefits for students’ focus and creativity, as well as their memory and executive function.
paragraphs.zh: 这包括有利于学生的注意力和创造力，以及他们的记忆和执行功能。

paragraphs.en: Some states, but not all, require recess
paragraphs.zh: 有些州，但不是所有的州，要求休会

paragraphs.en: Most states do not mandate that schools have recess every day or spell out a minimum amount of time students must spend moving their bodies.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数州并没有强制要求学校每天休息，也没有规定学生必须花在活动身体上的最低时间。

paragraphs.en: A 2025 report from the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health found that 11 states have laws addressing school recess. This ranges from Arizona’s requirement for 40 minutes of daily recess to Georgia, Indiana and Kentucky all requiring recess, but with no minimum duration.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰霍普金斯布隆伯格公共卫生学院2025年的一份报告发现，11个州都有关于学校休息的法律。从亚利桑那州要求每天休息40分钟到格鲁吉亚州、印第安纳州和肯塔基州都要求休息，但没有最短时间。

paragraphs.en: Massachusetts is one of the nearly 40 states without any laws regarding recess time. A recent article in The Boston Globe reported schools in Cambridge having 25 minutes of recess, while other schools across the state had only 15 minutes per day.
paragraphs.zh: 马萨诸塞州是近40个没有任何关于休息时间的法律的州之一。《波士顿地球仪》最近的一篇文章报道说，剑桥的学校每天有25分钟的休息时间，而全州其他学校每天只有15分钟。

paragraphs.en: Overall, there has been an uptick in state legislation aimed at preserving mandated daily school recess time, thanks partly to a new parent-led advocacy group called Say Yes to Recess. This group is pushing for schools across the country to provide a minimum of 60 minutes of protected school recess time each day.
paragraphs.zh: 总体而言，旨在保留强制性每日学校休息时间的州立法有所增加，这在一定程度上要归功于一个名为“对课间休息说是”的新的家长主导的倡导组织。该组织正在推动全国各地的学校每天提供至少60分钟的受保护的学校休息时间。

paragraphs.en: Started by three Tennessee moms, Say Yes to Recess has also helped advocate for Tennessee legislation that increased the state’s mandated daily school recess time from 15 to 40 minutes in July 2025.
paragraphs.zh: 由三位田纳西州的母亲发起，Say Yes to Recess还帮助倡导田纳西州立法，将该州规定的每日学校休息时间从2025年7月的15分钟增加到40分钟。

paragraphs.en: A moving target
paragraphs.zh: 一个移动的目标

paragraphs.en: During the 2001-02 school year, elementary school students from 349 school districts spent on average 36.8 minutes per day at recess.
paragraphs.zh: 在2001 - 2002学年，349个学区的小学生平均每天课间休息36.8分钟。

paragraphs.en: By 2025, the CDC found that students were spending 27 minutes on average in recess each day.
paragraphs.zh: 到2025年，疾病预防控制中心发现学生平均每天休息27分钟。

paragraphs.en: It’s also hard to track how much physical activity students get at school because public school districts and private schools often do not record and report this information.
paragraphs.zh: 此外，很难追踪学生在学校进行了多少体育活动，因为公立学区和私立学校通常不会记录和报告这些信息。

paragraphs.en: While the benefits of recess are not just isolated to young children, a 2026 international study showed that the amount of daily recess time across U.S. schools declines from a mean of 39.3 minutes per day for 6- to 7-year-olds to 24.5 minutes per day for 12- to 18-year-olds.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然课间休息的好处不仅仅局限于幼儿，但2026年的一项国际研究显示，美国学校每天的课间休息时间从6至7岁的平均39.3分钟下降到12至18岁的24.5分钟。

paragraphs.en: Making way for play
paragraphs.zh: 为玩耍让路

paragraphs.en: I conducted research at the Project Zero research center for creativity, ethics and the arts at Harvard University and highlighted the significance of play and the arts within urban public schools.
paragraphs.zh: 我在哈佛大学的创造力、道德和艺术研究中心进行了研究，并强调了游戏和艺术在城市公立学校中的重要性。

paragraphs.en: This 2024 study showed how play with materials supports both children’s and teachers’ creative learning. As someone who designs and studies children’s play spaces, I worry about what could happen if schools continue to reduce school recess because of staffing issues, budget cuts or prioritization of students’ preparation for high-stakes tests focused solely on literacy and numeracy.
paragraphs.zh: 这项2024年的研究表明，玩材料如何支持儿童和教师的创造性学习。作为一个设计和研究儿童游戏空间的人，我担心如果学校继续减少学校休息时间，因为人员问题，预算削减或优先考虑学生准备只关注识字和算术的高风险考试，会发生什么。

paragraphs.en: Research shows that this trend of not prioritizing recess could have significant effects on children’s and adolescents’ mental health, cognitive development and overall enjoyment of school.
paragraphs.zh: 研究表明，这种不重视课间休息的趋势可能会对儿童和青少年的心理健康、认知发展和学校的整体享受产生重大影响。

paragraphs.en: School are well intended but under strain
paragraphs.zh: 学校是好的，但压力很大

paragraphs.en: The decline in time for recess comes at a moment when many schools and districts are under increasing pressure as a result of declining student enrollment, pressure to meet state learning standards and budget cuts.
paragraphs.zh: 课间休息时间的减少正值许多学校和地区由于学生入学率下降、达到州学习标准的压力和预算削减而面临越来越大的压力之际。

paragraphs.en: For some schools, reduced staffing and the costs of maintaining outdoor play equipment to meet safety requirements have made it difficult to offer school recess.
paragraphs.zh: 对一些学校来说，由于人员减少和维护户外游乐设备以满足安全要求的费用，很难提供学校课间休息。

paragraphs.en: For other schools, an assumption that more time for instruction equals a higher-quality education may be driving decisions to minimize or eliminate time for unstructured play.
paragraphs.zh: 对于其他学校来说，更多的教学时间等于更高质量的教育的假设可能会促使他们决定尽量减少或消除非结构化游戏的时间。

paragraphs.en: Another factor that influences recess is when schools deny students recess time as a form of punishment – a policy that some scholars and educators are trying to block through legislation.
paragraphs.zh: 影响课间休息的另一个因素是学校拒绝学生课间休息作为一种惩罚形式--一些学者和教育工作者正试图通过立法来阻止这一政策。

paragraphs.en: As childhood health, social and cognitive research demonstrates, the amount of time school recess is given matters in children’s development as whole human beings. I believe it is up to schools, districts and parents to advocate for and ensure children’s right to protected school recess time every day.
paragraphs.zh: 正如儿童健康、社会和认知研究所表明的那样，学校休息时间的长短对儿童作为一个整体的发展至关重要。我认为，学校、地区和家长有责任倡导和确保儿童每天享有受保护的学校休息时间的权利。
